title: A welcome and a problem
prompt: Invent a short club or school story. Combine an interrupted past action with a completed event, describe a person’s behaviour, explain a small problem with an object and give two reasons for a choice.
checks: I used past simple and past continuous together.
I distinguished a finished past event from experience up to now.
I described behaviour without judging character from appearance.
I linked reasons clearly.

title: A practical plan
prompt: Invent a realistic goal and explain your plan. Include a decision made now, a prior intention, an arrangement with a time/date, a first conditional and a contrasting point.
checks: My future forms match their intended meanings.
I used present simple in the if-clause.
I used on, in and at appropriately.
My plan includes a specific goal and a time limit.

title: An imaginary place
prompt: Describe an imaginary place or club. Include two second-conditionals, one consequence with so ... that, a reflexive pronoun and two ways of adding information.
checks: I used past forms after if for imaginary situations.
I used would + base verb in the result.
My reflexive pronoun matches its subject.
I distinguished imaginary details from real predictions.

title: A model application
prompt: Write a fictional application to a named manager. Describe two relevant qualities, explain experience, use a gerund after a suitable expression and include one polite question. Do not include real contact details.
checks: My opening and closing suit a formal letter.
I used a gerund after involves, good at or interested in.
My personality words describe relevant behaviour.
This is a clearly fictional, unscored practice draft.

title: An imaginary journey and stay
prompt: Invent a journey and an accommodation booking. Include a ticket exchange, travel times and prepositions, two passive forms, a modal passive and a defining relative clause.
checks: My timetable and ticket details are consistent.
I used be + past participle in passive forms.
I used modal + be + past participle.
My relative pronoun refers clearly to a person or thing.

title: Report a fictional discussion
prompt: Invent a school-club discussion. Report two statements using says/said and told, include two indirect questions and use linkers to explain how an agreement was reached.
checks: My pronouns refer to the correct people.
I used said and told with the right patterns.
My indirect questions use statement word order.
My report represents each fictional person’s view clearly.
